title: Credit phasing & intervention playbook — trial cadence, expiry policies, and SQ automation
creator: Asha Gupta
description:
Overview: This ticket defines an experiment playbook to test a phased credit model (seed → sustain → expansion) combined with intelligent intervention triggers and automated Security Questionnaire (SQ) handoff for accounts that cross enterprise thresholds. Goal is to increase PLG trial-to-paid conversion while controlling free-tier unit economics and reducing manual contract/SQ work for Sales/RevOps.

Hypothesis: Introducing time-phased credit allocations plus targeted in-product and outbound interventions (based on usage velocity and feature signals) will increase 14-day and 30-day conversion rates by >= 15% for qualified leads while keeping cost-per-conversion under target. Automating SQ creation and pre-fill for qualifying accounts will reduce legal turnaround time by >= 40% and improve sales win-rate for enterprise-eligible trials.

Experiment design:
- Credit phases:
  - Seed (day 0–3): larger front-loaded allowance to drive meaningful usage and Aha moments.
  - Sustain (day 4–14): drip allowance tuned to encourage repeat engagement.
  - Expansion (day 15–30): conditional top-ups for accounts showing sustained activity or hitting Tier-1 API usage triggers.
- Expiry policies to test (A/B):
  - Fixed-window expiry (credits expire on day 30),
  - Sliding decay (credits decay weekly but accumulate partial carryover),
  - Soft-expiry with in-product warnings and micro-conversion prompts.
- Intervention mechanics:
  - Real-time triggers: usage velocity, embedding calls, model latency anomalies, and feature adoption (e.g., dedicated endpoint requests).
  - In-product hooks: contextual banners, 'task-first' templates that map to paid value, and a single-click upgrade CTA prefilled with org info.
  - Outbound: triggered email series and Slack/GTM outreach to Sales when enterprise thresholds are crossed.
- SQ automation:
  - When account meets enterprise criteria (quota, allowed IP ranges, contract value estimate), system auto-creates an SQ intake with prefilled org data, attaches recent logs & consent statement, and notifies Legal via Slack + Jira ticket.
  - Implement a webhook to the contracts intake service and a lightweight template for Sales to review.

Instrumentation & success metrics:
- Primary metrics: 14d and 30d conversion rate (trial -> paid), cost per conversion, ARPA uplift for converted accounts.
- Secondary metrics: time-to-first-value (TTFV), engaged days per trial, support/infra cost delta, SQ turnaround time, legal touch count.
- Events to instrument: credit_issued, credit_consumed, credit_expired, intervention_shown, intervention_clicked, upgrade_completed, sq_created, sq_accepted, sales_contacted.

Rollout plan & Phases:
1) Spike & design (2 sprints): finalize phase sizes, expiry variants, intervention creatives, acceptance criteria; design microcopy and banners.
2) Implementation (3 sprints): engineers implement credit scheduler, expiry engine, intervention gating, SQ webhook; design implements banners & templates.
3) Canary (2 weeks): 5% of new signups; monitor cost signals and conversion lift.
4) Ramp to 25% then 100% based on safety gates.

Safety gates & guardrails:
- Daily cost cap per experiment cohort; auto-disable if unit cost exceeds target.
- Rate limits on SQ automation to avoid Legal inundation; buffer queue for manual review.
- Privacy checks: ensure prefill data excludes PII beyond business contact details; legal checklist must be completed before auto-submission.

Acceptance criteria:
- Experiment infra functioning end-to-end and instrumented.
- No >10% increase in infra/support costs for cohort during canary.
- Clear >=15% relative lift in 30-day conversion in a statistically significant sample OR plan documented for iterative changes.
- SQ automation reduces manual intake time by >=40% in pilot accounts.

Open questions / risks: 
- Optimal seed/sustain/expansion sizes vs. model costs (need eng sim of token spend).
- Potential perception of 'gaming' credits leading to superficial usage; how to detect low-quality signal.
- Legal appetite for automated SQ submission; need sign-off on template from Legal.
- Measurement: need reliable attribution from multi-channel interventions (in-product + email + sales).
